candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Értesítő (Hungarian Public Procurement Bulletin, daily signed PDF issues)
candidates.why_relevant: Legally mandated official gazette of Hungarian public procurement. Every national-threshold notice from state banks' owners, MÁK, ministries, municipalities and state-owned companies buying payment/banking IT (számlavezetés, POS terminál, pénzforgalmi rendszer) appears here, including CPV codes, budget, award and delivery deadlines. Daily issues are published as signed PDFs (e.g. KE-2025-159.pdf), making bulk longitudinal collection feasible.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Daily fetch of the issue PDF index (pattern https://www.kozbeszerzes.hu/media/issue/pdf/signed/KE-YYYY-NN.pdf), PDF text extraction, then CPV + keyword filtering (66xxxxxx financial services, 72xxxxxx IT services, 30144200/302xxxxx terminals).
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search on seed query + snowball from search result PDFs
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Értesítő ajánlati felhívás pénzforgalmi rendszer bank informatikai beszerzés

candidates.source_name: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (KBA) – notice search interface, Közbeszerzési Hatóság
candidates.why_relevant: Structured, queryable central register of procurement notices and contracts (including below-threshold summaries). Supports saved searches with daily e-mail alerts — a ready-made monitoring channel for keywords like 'pénzforgalmi', 'kártyaelfogadás', 'core banking', 'terminál'.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Registered saved-search alerts plus periodic scripted query of the search endpoint; parse result lists into a notice register keyed by ajánlatkérő + CPV.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language search for the national procurement database
queries_used: Közbeszerzési Adatbázis kozbeszerzes.hu adatbázis szerződések kereső hirdetmény API

candidates.source_name: EKR – Elektronikus Közbeszerzési Rendszer, public notice board (hirdetmények)
candidates.why_relevant: The mandatory end-to-end platform where Hungarian contracting authorities run procedures; the public 'hirdetmények' view exposes live calls and, crucially, the procurement documentation (közbeszerzési dokumentáció, műszaki leírás) that contains the actual technical/compliance requirements driving payment-system change. Structured search was upgraded in June 2024.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Scheduled scrape/browse of the public hirdetmények search with CPV and keyword filters; download attached műszaki leírás PDFs for requirement extraction. Session/JS-heavy portal — headless browser likely needed.
candidates.discovered_via_method: hu-language seed query on EKR

candidates.source_name: TED – Tenders Electronic Daily (EU OJ Supplement), Hungary above-threshold notices
candidates.why_relevant: All Hungarian above-threshold contracts (services ~EUR 140k+, and utilities/works thresholds) must be published here in a standardised eForms structure, in English as well as Hungarian. This is the cleanest machine-readable route to large state banking/payments IT tenders and their award values and deadlines.

candidates.source_name: Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség (DKÜ) Zrt. – central government IT procurement body
candidates.why_relevant: Under Government Decree 301/2018 (XII.27) most state bodies must route IT procurement exclusively through DKÜ. Any state-sector banking/payments IT buy therefore passes through DKÜ's framework agreements — making DKÜ a mandatory gatekeeper and an early indicator of state IT demand and of which vendors hold framework positions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor /hirek/ and /kozerdeku-adatok/ for framework agreements and annual reports; monitor kozbeszerzes.dkuzrt.hu for DKÜ's own procurement procedures. The IDPR application (idpr.dkuzrt.hu) is credentialed and out of scope for collection.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated, publicly documented REST/JSON API was found for the Hungarian Közbeszerzési Adatbázis (KBA) or for EKR. Searches surfaced only web search interfaces, saved-search e-mail alerts and PDF issues.
negative_findings.result_summary: Machine-readable national-level access appears to be limited to TED (for above-threshold notices) and third-party re-publishers such as Opentender; national below-threshold data likely requires HTML scraping or PDF parsing of the Közbeszerzési Értesítő.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for this cell must budget for scraping/PDF extraction rather than assuming an official API; this affects reliability and maintenance cost of the pipeline.

negative_findings.description: Searching in Hungarian for Magyar Posta public procurement procedures specifically for pénzforgalmi (payment) services returned mainly the company's ÁSZF/terms and fee announcements, not procurement notices.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only a generic 'Beszerzések, pályázatok' landing page was identified; no payment-systems-specific Magyar Posta tender was located in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Magyar Posta's status as an in-scope contracting entity for payment-related buys is asserted by the cell rationale but not yet evidenced with a concrete notice; needs targeted confirmation via EKR/TED buyer search before relying on it.

negative_findings.description: No page fetches were performed in this pass; all candidates come from search-engine result metadata and snippets. No URL in this slice should be treated as liveness-verified.
negative_findings.result_summary: URLs are recorded with confidence scores only; EKR in particular is a JavaScript/session-heavy portal likely to resist simple fetching.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The deterministic verification pass must resolve every URL; a failure on ekr.gov.hu should be treated as a bot-defence hypothesis, not as a dead source.

negative_findings.description: GIRO Zrt. (operator of the Hungarian interbank clearing system, MNB-owned) was hypothesised as a public-sector-adjacent buyer of payment infrastructure, but no procurement-publication route for it was located in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: No GIRO procurement page or notice was found; whether GIRO qualifies as a contracting entity under the Kbt. remains unconfirmed.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: GIRO procurements would be among the highest-value payment-infrastructure signals in Hungary; a confirmed publication route would materially strengthen this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: State-owned or state-influenced banks and payment operators (e.g. MBH Bank, Magyar Bankholding-successor entities, Eximbank, MFB, GIRO Zrt., Takarék/Posta partner arrangements) were not systematically checked for contracting-entity status and publication routes.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated buyer-name sweep in EKR and TED using each entity's exact legal name as ajánlatkérő, and check each entity's own site for a 'közbeszerzés'/'beszerzés' section.

coverage_gaps.description: No CPV-code map was built for this cell. Effective filtering of KÉ/EKR/TED depends on the right CPV families (66100000 banking/financial services, 66172000 payment transaction processing, 72xxxxxx IT services, 30144200 terminals, 48xxxxxx software).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Build and validate a CPV allow-list against the Közbeszerzési Hatóság CPV code tool, then hard-code it into the collection filters.

coverage_gaps.description: Municipal (önkormányzati) buyers were sampled only via examples (Józsefváros 2021, BKK). With decentralised municipal account-keeping starting 1 October 2025, the municipal tender wave is a major expected signal but has no systematic watchlist.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Create a saved KBA/EKR search on 'számlavezetés' + 'pénzforgalmi számla' restricted to önkormányzat/önkormányzati buyers, and set up daily alerting from Q4 2025 onward.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language coverage of this cell is effectively limited to TED; national below-threshold Hungarian notices exist only in Hungarian, and EKR documentation attachments are Hungarian-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Plan for HU-language NLP/keyword extraction and machine translation in the pipeline; do not rely on English-only monitoring for this cell.

coverage_gaps.description: Forward-looking signals (annual közbeszerzési terv documents, DKÜ framework pipelines, előzetes tájékoztató / prior information notices) were identified only for MÁK and NISZ; other buyers' procurement plans were not enumerated.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically harvest annual 'közbeszerzési terv' PDFs from each watchlisted buyer's Üvegzseb/közadat page each January and after each modification, since these precede notices by 6-12 months.

brief: Hungary's public-sector procurement route for banking and payments intelligence rests on three mandatory, mutually reinforcing publication layers: the national Közbeszerzési Értesítő (daily signed PDF issues) with its searchable Közbeszerzési Adatbázis, the EKR e-procurement platform that additionally exposes the technical documentation behind each call, and TED for above-threshold notices in machine-readable eForms. Around this core sit the key buyers and gatekeepers — Magyar Államkincstár (whose decentralised municipal account-keeping change from 1 October 2025 should trigger a wave of számlavezetés tenders), the Digitális Kormányzati Ügynökség as the compulsory channel for state IT buys, plus MNB, NISZ, NAV and Magyar Posta, each with its own Üvegzseb/közadat disclosure page carrying forward-looking annual procurement plans. Secondary layers add interpretive value: the Közbeszerzési Döntőbizottság decision database exposes contested technical requirements in credit-institution IT tenders, while Opentender and investigative outlets such as Átlátszó help with vendor-concentration and pricing analysis. The main constraints are the absence of an official national API (PDF and HTML extraction will be required), Hungarian-only content below the EU thresholds, and unconfirmed publication routes for state-adjacent payment operators such as GIRO Zrt.
